A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same premise-verification framework. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching retained material across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original KG-FPQ premise-detection and hallucination-mitigation experiments, including retrieval comparisons, three-model accuracy results and single-hop versus multi-hop analysis.

after.justification: V2 retains original experiments and reports additional benchmark evaluations, component ablations, human validation, longer-query tests and computational measurements.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same logical-form extraction, retrieval, premise classification and conditional warning before answering. The extraction model, encoder and warning text remain unchanged. Added evaluations do not document a new algorithmic component or redesigned procedure.

E1.justification: V1 evaluates KG-FPQ art-domain yes/no questions. V2 adds CREAK entity-grounded commonsense claims, FEVER verification using Wikipedia text, and longer KG-FPQ queries preserving the original premises (Tables 3–4 and Appendix A.5). These substantially broaden task and input coverage.

E2.justification: V2 newly evaluates SAC3 for premise detection (Table 16), Direct RAG for hallucination mitigation (Table 6), and Contrastive Decoding (Tables 5 and 18). The original retrieval and prompting comparators remain.

E3.justification: The reported main detection model changes from GPT-3.5-turbo to GPT-4o-mini, with additional Llama-3.1 detection evaluations. Mitigation expands from three to six LLMs. New protocols include two annotators grading 100 sampled logical forms each, rewriting the first 105 KG-FPQ questions, and a hardware-specific runtime comparison.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained stage-use comparisons, hop analysis and case study, v2 adds relation/entity-removal ablations (Tables 12–14), premise-specific error breakdowns (Table 11), human logical-form validation, longer-query robustness tests and computational-cost analysis. These investigate component necessity, error sources and practical behavior previously unexamined.

E5.justification: V2 introduces paired t-tests across configurations with reported p-values (Tables 7–8) and inter-annotator agreement of 1.0 (Appendix A.6). V1 reports neither. Neither version supplies repeated-run counts, seeds or confidence intervals; the new tests do not establish increased experimental repetition, and their sampling units remain underspecified.

E6.justification: V2 adds extensive benchmark, model, ablation, validation and timing results. Its main G-retriever results report F1 97.12% and accuracy 95.24% with GPT-4o-mini; v1's GPT-3.5 results of 84.47% and 79.37% remain in v2 Table 17, so this is not a same-setting gain. Original three-model mitigation scores remain, while reported Perplexity AI accuracy changes from 92.4% to 91.4%.

T1.justification: Section 5.1 adds an O(k+s) overhead claim, defining retrieved-candidate count k and feature size s, without a derivation or proof. Existing premise definitions, retrieval maximizations and conditional prompt update remain mathematically equivalent despite renumbering and shorthand notation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contributions and conclusion retain the same central claims: logical forms support premise verification, explicit premise warnings mitigate hallucination, and the framework avoids logit access and large-scale fine-tuning. Additional evidence does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations concerning Direct RAG's semantic mismatch, complementary logical-form components, effectiveness beyond graph knowledge sources, and potential use in sensitive dialogue. It removes v1's explicit limitations discussion covering answer biases, knowledge-graph availability and maintenance, and restriction to discriminative tasks.

D1.justification: V2 adds the logical-form conversion prompt, temperature=0 and top_p=1 settings, workstation and timing hardware, and Perplexity AI's GPT-4-Omni backend. Appendix A.5 supplies a repository link for rewriting prompts and longer-query materials. These are additional disclosures; they do not establish changes to previously undisclosed settings or verify external resource availability.

R1.justification: Related work gains a Logical Forms discussion covering LINC, Logic-LM and SymbCoT, alongside references for new datasets, models and SAC3. Table 1 and Section 5.1 substantially expand positioning against post-hoc approaches through training-cost, efficiency and compatibility comparisons.

P1.justification: The six main sections and much original prose remain. V2 makes targeted condensations, renames baseline subsections as methods, places metrics within the corresponding task subsections, and reorganizes the expanded appendix. The main narrative sequence remains stable.

P2.justification: V2 adopts TMLR typography, author formatting and headers; replaces Figure 1's film example with a medical example; and revises Figure 4's scale and placement. Numerous new tables present added analyses, while the mitigation table gains model rows and a Direct RAG column. V1's radar visualization is retained as Figure 5 alongside an updated main Figure 3.

improvement.justification: V2 addresses v1's narrow validation with broader benchmarks, controls, ablations and reproducibility details. However, new reporting conflicts weaken confidence: Tables 5–6 give Llama-3.1 'Ours' accuracy as 89.5%, versus 86.7% in Table 18 without an explained setting difference; Table 7 lists G-retriever versus wRAG in both directions with different p-values. Explicit limitations are also removed. The PDFs do not resolve these discrepancies sufficiently to determine whether the expanded evidence yields a net quality improvement.
